subject: Inference hosting & migration constraints — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily@horizon-labs.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-22T13:04:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: inference hosting and migration constraints

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo today — helpful overview. A few clarifying questions from our infra/ML platform side so we can decide hosting direction (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC / on-prem):

- Current infra: we run two legacy GPU clusters (NVIDIA V100) behind an internal inference API; peak steady qps ~65, occasional spikes to ~220 for short bursts.
- Data residency: customer PII must stay in our US-only VPC; some telemetry can leave.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 220ms for typical chat workflows (history ~1.5k tokens).
- Throughput: batch scoring for nightly reranks (~30k docs) and near-real-time chat for product features.

Questions:
1) For migration from our legacy on-prem clusters, do you recommend a lift-and-shift to Dedicated reserved pools or a staged approach (Hosted for eval, then Dedicated/Private for production)?
2) If we need Private VPC (customer-managed), how tightly integrated is the control plane and what are the onboarding timelines you typically see?
3) Any common blockers when customers come from custom self-hosted LLM stacks (custom KV cache, model variants, quantized weights)?

I can attach our infra diagram if that helps. Would also appreciate a rough cost/throughput rubric to start the procurement conversation.

—Emily
Emily Stone
Head of Platform Engineering, Horizon Labs

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stone <emily@horizon-labs.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-22T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference hosting and migration constraints

Emily — really useful detail, thanks. Quick recap from our side and a proposed next-step plan. I've attached a short migration intake form to capture a few more specifics (Horizon_Migration_Form.pdf).

Short answers to your questions and hypothesis-driven plan:

1) Recommendation (high level):
   - Stage 0 (eval): Hosted API for a 2–4 week technical POC to validate latencies, throughput envelope, and correctness against your rerank/prompt sets. Low friction, no infra changes.
   - Stage 1 (scale/isolated): If you need predictable throughput and VPC isolation, move to Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) with private peering. This preserves performance and gives predictable unit costs.
   - Stage 2 (locked/regulatory): For strict policy or air-gapped needs, Redwood Private (customer-controlled VPC / on-prem package). More onboarding but required for full data residency.

   Rationale: customers migrating from legacy GPU clusters often want to prove model parity and latency on Hosted before committing to Dedicated capacity. Private is typically pursued when procurement/legal requires it.

2) Private VPC onboarding timeline / control plane:
   - Typical timeline: 4–8 weeks for standard Private VPC onboarding (depends on customer SSO/KMS/HSM integration and networking approvals).
   - Control plane: customer controls network peering and KMS keys; we provide a lightweight agent and a customer-managed subnet. Audit logs and token-level tracing are forwarded to your SIEM if requested.

3) Common blockers from self-hosted stacks:
   - KV cache compatibility and cache warming (we can import snapshots, but format matters).
   - Custom quantized artifacts (some models need re-quantization or a compatible execution path).
   - Proprietary tooling around batching — our runtime handles continuous batching but integration work is occasionally needed for custom request headers/metadata.

Questions for you (short list we need answers to before design):
- Can you share a sample prompt/rerank set and a 30-minute capture of typical request distribution?
- Do you require FIPS/KMS/HSM integrations?
- Who is the procurement contact and expected contract timeline (Q4/2027 target)?

Proposed next steps (mutual action items):
- You: fill the migration intake form (attached) + drop your infra diagram (horizon_arch_diag.png) to the Drive link.
- Us: we run a Hosted POC (1–4 weeks) using a mirror of traffic for latency + rerank correctness; provide a Dedicated sizing estimate and a private-VPC onboarding sketch.
- Schedule: Do you have a 45-minute slot next week for a technical handoff with Neha (solutions eng) and Rishi (deploy lead)? We can propose Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Cost ballpark: based on what you shared (steady 65 qps, bursts to 220, batch rerank job), a conservative estimate:
- Hosted POC: minimal usage costs + support hours (~$3–5k for the POC week depending on tokens).
- Dedicated (reserved): depends on GPU class; for 220-peak bursts with headroom, estimate 2–3 A100 equivalent pods (we'll provide exact sizing after perf run).

Attachments: Horizon_Migration_Form.pdf (fill and return)

Looking forward to next steps — happy to sync.

—Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Follow-up: inference hosting and migration constraints — proposed MA Plan & checklist

Emily / Sara — looping procurement and putting a concise mutual-action plan up front. Also copied Neha and Rishi for the technical handoff.

Short checklist for traffic mirror scrub before Hosted POC ingestion:
- Remove or tokenise any PII fields (names, SSNs) — we can provide a small sanitiser script.
- Keep conversation context length to 2k tokens max for the POC capture to reflect likely production history windows.
- Add request metadata headers: x-horizon-request-id, x-client-tenant (we use these for tracing), and anonymize user ids.
- Provide a 1-hour and a 24-hour capture so we can model burst vs steady states.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
1) Horizon: return filled intake form + scrubbed captures to the Drive link (due: 2027-08-27).
2) Redwood: provision Hosted POC environment, run perf/latency tests, and deliver sizing + Dedicated estimate (due: 2027-09-03).
3) Horizon: procurement kickoff with Sara (target: decision by 2027-12-15).

Meeting windows proposed for tech handoff: Tue 2027-08-30 14:00–14:45 PST or Wed 2027-08-31 15:00–15:45 PST — please confirm preferred slot.

Open items we will clarify in the handoff: KV cache snapshot format, model artifact packaging (are quantized weights in standard BF16/INT8?), and any required logging retention policies.

If this looks good I will raise DEAL-78921 as an internal opportunity and scope a minimal SOW for the POC week.

Best,
Jonas
